info.title: Convex Deployment API
info.description: Admin API for interacting with deployments.

post.description:
Update one or many environment variables in a deployment.
This will invalidate all subscriptions, since environment variables
are accessible in queries but are not part of the cache key of a query
result.

get.description:
Get all environment variables in a deployment.
In the future this might not include "secret" environment
variables.

List a deployment's audit log events on or after a timestamp, from least to
most recent. Pass the returned `cursor` (along with the same `from`) to
fetch the next page.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Only return events on or after this time, in milliseconds since epoch.
Pass the same value on every page of a paginated request.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return (defaults to 15, capped at 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page.

get.description: Returns identity information about this deployment.

The reported usage is only guaranteed to reflect the full window when
`seedStatus` is `complete`. A `pending` or `partial` status means the
backfill is still in progress and the returned usage may understate actual
usage, so retry later for an accurate total.

post.description:
Disables a deployment without deleting any data. The deployment will not
operate until it is unpaused. While a deployment is paused, new functions
calls will return an error, scheduled jobs will queue and run when the
deployment is resumed, and cron jobs will be skipped. This means that no
function calls or bandwidth usage will be charged while the deployment is
paused, but storage costs will still apply.

Reenables a deployment that was previously paused. The deployment will
resume normal operation, including any scheduled jobs that were queued while
paused.

Paginated streamable export of some or all of a deployment's data.

Call this endpoint repeatedly, passing the opaque `pagination.nextCursor`
from each response back in the next request as `cursor`. Omit `cursor` on
the first call.

Apply each page's `truncates` before its `values`, and persist these changes
atomically with `pagination.nextCursor`. Retrying the same input cursor may
return a different page, so non-atomic updates can lead to data
inconsistency.

To do a one time data sync, keep fetching pages until reaching an `upToDate`
page. For a continuous streaming export, continue fetching pages
periodically. It's recommended to sleep between `upToDate` pages to reduce
overhead.

The caller must have the `deployment:data:view` permission.

get.description:
Returns the progress of active data sync (/v1/data/sync).

A data sync is considered active for 3 days after the most recent API call.
from `/data/sync` within the past 3 days.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of syncs to return (defaults to 50, capped at 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page.

get.description:
Returns the progress of a single data sync (/v1/data/sync), identified by
the `syncId` that endpoint returns. The status is the same one
`/data/list_active_syncs` reports for each sync it lists.

A data sync is considered active for 3 days after the most recent API call
from `/data/sync`. Ids of syncs that are unknown or no longer active return
a 404.

The caller must have the `deployment:data:view` permission.

parameters.name: sync_id
parameters.description: `syncId` of the sync, as returned by /data/sync

ActiveDataSync.description:
The status of one active data sync, as of its most recent page. Returned
by `/api/v1/data/sync/{syncId}` and for each sync listed by
`/api/v1/data/list_active_syncs`.

syncId.description:
Unique id of the sync, assigned when it started (i.e. when
`/api/v1/data/sync` was called without a cursor) and stable across its
pages.

lastUpdated.description:
Wall-clock time of the last `/data/sync` call made by this sync, as a
unix timestamp in milliseconds.

status.description: The sync's progress as of its most recently recorded page.

ActiveDataSyncSnapshotting.description:
The sync is still traversing its selected tables; the data returned so
far is not yet a consistent snapshot.

oneOf.description:
The literal string `snapshotting`, discriminating "snapshotting" status
objects.

numTablesSynced.description: Tables whose initial traversal has completed.

totalTables.description: Total tables selected for the sync.

currentComponent.description:
The component of the table currently being traversed (the empty
string for the root component).

numDocumentsInCurrentTable.description: Documents synced so far from the current table.

totalDocumentsInCurrentTable.description: Total documents in the current table, as of a recent snapshot.

numDocumentsSynced.description:
Documents synced over the sync's lifetime, including deletions and
re-synced revisions of documents that changed mid-sync — so this can
slightly exceed `totalDocuments`.

totalDocuments.description: Total documents across all selected tables, as of a recent snapshot.

ActiveDataSyncStale.description:
The sync reached a consistent snapshot at `syncedTs`, but its timestamp is
stale; it is streaming later changes (CDC). Newer data may be available.

oneOf.description: The literal string `stale`, discriminating "stale" status objects.

totalTables.description: Total tables selected for the sync.

numDocumentsSynced.description:
Documents synced over the sync's lifetime, including deletions and
re-synced revisions.

syncedTs.description: The database timestamp at which the synced data is consistent.

oneOf.description:
The sync has not yet reached a consistent snapshot. The entries emitted
so far are an incomplete initial traversal of the selected tables.
Syncs begin in this state, and may reenter this state if tables are
added/replaced

The entries emitted so far represent a consistent snapshot at
a stale `snapshotTs`. The sync is "catching up".
The sync is up to date and represents a latest consistent snapshot.

ActiveDataSyncStatus.description: The progress of an active data sync, discriminated by `type`.

ActiveDataSyncUpToDate.description:
The sync reached a consistent snapshot at `syncedTs` and has caught up to
the latest data.

oneOf.description: The literal string `upToDate`, discriminating "up to date" status objects.

totalTables.description: Total tables selected for the sync.

numDocumentsSynced.description:
Documents synced over the sync's lifetime, including deletions and
re-synced revisions.

syncedTs.description: The database timestamp at which the synced data is consistent.

DataSyncArgs.description: Arguments to the data sync (streaming export) API (`/api/v1/data/sync`).

cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous call. Omit to start from scratch.

selection.description:
When set, only sync the selected subset of the data.

Selects the components, tables, and columns to export. Each key is a
component path (`""` for the root component), mapped to the selection
for that component.

The selection may change between calls of the same sync: newly selected
tables are synced from scratch, possibly moving the sync into
`snapshotting` state if necessary, and emit a truncate on the first page
they appear so the consumer starts them from a clean slate. Deselected
tables stop being synced.

DataSyncResponse.description: One page returned by the data sync API.

status.description: The status of the sync after this page.

truncates.description:
Tables truncated by this page. The consumer should drop everything it
previously synced for each table, then apply `values` (which re-sync
them from scratch). Logically applies before `values`.

A table is truncated whenever it (re)enters the export from scratch —
the first page it is synced (including on a cold start), when it is
newly selected, or when it is replaced by a bulk operation such as
`npx convex import`.

values.description: Documents created, updated, or deleted in this page.

syncId.description:
Unique id of the sync, assigned on the first page and stable across
the sync's lifetime. Identifies this sync in `/data/sync/{syncId}` and
`/data/list_active_syncs`.

pagination.description:
Pagination information. The data sync endpoint is an infinite streaming
endpoint, so `nextCursor` is always present and `hasMore` is always
`true` — another page can always be fetched with the cursor. Use
`status` to pace calls: back off significantly to wait for more writes
once it reports `upToDate`.

DataSyncSnapshotting.description:
The sync has not yet reached a consistent snapshot. The entries emitted
so far are an incomplete initial traversal of the selected tables.
Syncs begin in this state. The sync's
progress can be monitored via `/data/sync/{syncId}` or
`/data/list_active_syncs`, keyed by the response's `syncId`. Syncs may
return to this state if the table selection has changes that requires large
data sync.

oneOf.description:
The literal string `snapshotting`, discriminating "snapshotting" status
objects.

DataSyncStale.description:
The entries emitted so far represent a consistent snapshot at
a stale `snapshotTs`.

oneOf.description: The literal string `stale`, discriminating "stale" status objects.

snapshotTs.description: The database timestamp at which the synced data is consistent.

DataSyncStatus.description:
The consistency state reported alongside a data sync page, discriminated
by `type`.

DataSyncTruncate.description:
An entry indicating that the table should be truncated. Emitted when a table
is newly syncing or replaced wholesale (e.g. by `npx convex import`).
Reported separately from `values` since it carries none of the per-document
fields.

component.description: The path of the component the table is in.

table.description: The name of the truncated table.

DataSyncUpToDate.description:
The sync is up to date and represents a latest consistent snapshot.
For a streaming export in this state, it is recommended to backoff for
some time, wait for more data, and then continue the streaming sync.

oneOf.description: The literal string `upToDate`, discriminating "up to date" status objects.

snapshotTs.description: The database timestamp at which the synced data is consistent.

DataSyncValue.description:
A single document-level entry emitted by the data sync API: a Convex
document (or a tombstone, for a deletion) nested under `value`, with
metadata fields alongside it.

component.description: The path of the component this entry is from.

table.description: The name of the table this entry is from.

ts.description: The timestamp at which this revision was written.

deleted.description: Whether the document was deleted (a tombstone).

value.description:
The fields of the document, including the built-in `_id` and
`_creationTime`. For `deleted` documents, only `_id` is present.

Optional comma-separated list of tags. These are sent to Datadog in each
log event via the `ddtags` field.

service.description: Service name used as a special tag in Datadog.

SeedStatusResponse.description:
Progress of the historical-usage backfill. Only `complete` guarantees the
reported usage reflects the full window. While the status is `pending` or
`partial`, history from before this deployment was loaded may not be
hydrated yet and the numbers can understate actual usage, so retry later for
an accurate total. `failed` means the backfill couldn't hydrate any history.
